old_value: {"id":"vouch-faq3","title":"git-vouch-trqp: TRQP bridge so OpenVTC verify-trust can check git-vouch signers","description":"A separate, optional service (NOT part of the git-vouch single file, which stays a CLI with no service) that answers ToIP TRQP authorization queries from a git-vouch registry, so OpenVTC's verify-trust and other TRQP consumers can ask 'may this DID sign for the kernel?'. Facts from source (2026-10-22): verify-trust resolves a registry DID and picks TSP\u003eDIDComm\u003eHTTPS from its DID document, so HTTPS alone suffices; HTTPS answers are unsigned, trust rests on the DID-document-bound endpoint (~/GIT/OpenVTC_verifiable-git-infrastructure/crates/verify-trust/src/registry.rs:185-260). Query = {entity_id: signer DID, authority_id, action, resource(forge-qualified)} (src/lib.rs:1-45, src/resource.rs). Signer DID comes from the commit committer header; DID doc must publish the Ed25519 key in the sshsig. TRQP spec: ~/PROJECT/ToIP/spec/toip-trqp.md. Design constraint: the service is a thin stateless shim over 'git vouch query'; git-vouch stays the single source of truth for tier logic.","status":"open","priority":3,"issue_type":"epic","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T16:32:58.920669457Z","created_by":"agent","updated_at":"2026-10-22T16:32:58.920669457Z"}
new_value: {"notes":"DECIDED (Mark, 2026-10-22): git-vouch's key types are fixed by the kernel and not negotiable for interop: ssh-ed25519, sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com (kernel.org's default FIDO type), ecdsa-sha2-nistp256, sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com. OpenVTC's verify-trust must accept them (today it accepts only plain ssh-ed25519: VGI verify-trust/src/lib.rs:941-950; vgi-core/src/did.rs:10,41-44; vgi-core/src/sshsig.rs:1). Bridge work stays parked until OpenVTC moves, a real consumer asks, and an LF operator owns it (Claude's verdict 2026-10-22: reasonable to plan, premature to build). Draft message to OpenVTC in session scratchpad; not sent."}
